- Key features: Mottled appearance with grayish-white powdery or sooty coating on leaf surface; no prominent sunken lesions visible; overall leaf color is maintained but dulled by the coating

Since this is a leaf, all 4 classes are candidates. Now I'll view one reference from each class to narrow down.

**Initial assessment:**
- **Anthracnose (ref)**: Dark brown lesions with severe damage - doesn't match test
- **Die_Back (ref)**: Severely withered dark leaf - doesn't match test
- **Powdery_Mildew (ref)**: White/pale powdery coating - **very similar to test**
- **Sooty_Mould (ref)**: Dark black spots - different from test (test has pale coating)

The test image's pale/whitish coating is most consistent with Powdery_Mildew. Let me view additional references to confirm. I have 4 views remaining.

| Class | Visual Features | Comparison to Test |
|-------|---|---|
| **Powdery_Mildew** | Pale/white powdery coating scattered across leaf surface (3 refs) | ✅ Excellent match - same whitish coating pattern |
| **Sooty_Mould** | Dark brown/blackish specks and patches (3 refs) | ✗ Different - test image coating is pale, not dark |
| **Anthracnose** | Dark brown lesions, severe damage | ✗ Different - no prominent dark lesions in test |
| **Die_Back** | Severely withered, dark, collapsed leaf | ✗ Different - test leaf maintains structure |

**Key distinguishing feature:** The test image shows a **pale/whitish** powdery coating on an otherwise intact green leaf. This matches all Powdery_Mildew references and contrasts sharply with Sooty_Mould's **dark/blackish** appearance.
